conventions.convention: Tau is the least integer Alexander sublevel whose inclusion has nonzero image in the one-dimensional total hat homology over F₂. The standard unknot generator has Alexander level zero.

The reverse mirror is the image under the fixed orientation-reversing reflection with knot orientation subsequently reversed. The finite dual filtration consists of functionals annihilating F_{−s−1}C.
Tensor products use the convolution filtration F_s(C⊗D)=Σ_{p+q≤s}F_pC⊗F_qD.

The geometric connected-sum, cobordism and main tau results explicitly assume countable choice. The genus is smooth, in the standard four-ball, with connected compact oriented proper spanning surfaces.
Setting U=0 in a staircase means quotienting its specified polynomial minus lattice by U; it does not mean specializing the Laurent coefficient ring.
The counterexample uses Hedden–Ording's positive-clasped Whitehead double with twist parameter t=2, and rational Lee homology normalized by s=s_max−1.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice. For smooth oriented knots K,J with the stated Seifert normalizations, CFK∞(K#J) is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to CFK∞(K)⊗CFK∞(J), with filtration-preserving equivalence and homotopies. The normalized finite hat complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to C_K⊗C_J. Consequently τ(K#J)=τ(K)+τ(J).
Assume countable choice. The common normalized filtered knot Floer threshold is diagram-independent and invariant under smooth concordance; τ(K#J)=τ(K)+τ(J), and |τ(K)|≤g₄ˢᵐ(K).
Assume countable choice. A connected compact smooth oriented genus-g surface properly embedded in S³×[0,1], with product collars and oriented boundary −K₀⊔K₁, satisfies |τ(K₁)−τ(K₀)|≤g.

For finite integer-filtered chain complexes C,D over F₂ with increasing bounded exhaustive subcomplex filtrations and H(C)≅H(D)≅F₂, the convolution-filtered tensor product has H(C⊗D)≅F₂ and τ(C⊗D)=τ(C)+τ(D).

For the supplied regular normalized diagram and corresponding reverse-mirror diagram, the latter's finite filtered hat complex is filtered chain isomorphic to the dual with complementary annihilator filtration; its diagramwise tau is the negative of the original tau.
The standard genus-zero one-pointed unknot diagram has normalized total hat homology F₂ generated at Alexander filtration zero, and its diagramwise tau threshold is zero.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 says, “On the reflected surface −Σ use the reflected almost-complex structure −J_t and define u†(s,t)=u(−s,t),” and identifies this diagram with the reverse mirror. With unchanged attaching systems and marks, that operation produces (−Σ,α,β,w,z), representing the mirror with transported knot orientation, rather than the reverse mirror under the stated w-to-z alpha-arc convention. The attaching-system/mark transformation implementing the additional knot-orientation reversal is missing. This distinction is explicit in the opened supplier lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap, Proof 2.1–4.1, which uses (Σ,β,α,w,z) for reverse-mirror duality. Hom's cited statement supplies filtered chain homotopy equivalence, so it alone does not justify the stronger literal isomorphism asserted for the unspecified reflected diagram. The intended standard duality is supported, but the actual diagram identification needs clarification.

seams_checked.note: The owned claims retain smooth oriented surfaces, standard ambient manifolds, connectedness, product collars, the smooth genus minimum and countable choice. No topological concordance or locally flat genus conclusion is inferred.

The finite threshold requires one-dimensional total homology. The examples distinguish the polynomial lattice quotient from Laurent specialization and avoid applying tau directly to unreduced multipointed complexes. The opened Hom survey confirms the trefoil staircase and threshold convention.

The genus-difference proof uses explicitly imported Hom concordance/genus results and a cut-arc construction. It does not infer nonvanishing or a genus filtration shift merely from existence or naturality of decorated cobordism maps.

The actual tensor equivalence, grading conventions and tau formulas are cited faithfully. However, the opened direct consumers omit the supplier's explicit countable-choice hypothesis from their Statements and Given sections while acknowledging that branch in axiom_use; the precise presentation findings are routed in alerts.
